notes: Example configuration generated by the CraneCalc configurator; fictitious crane, supplier, site and owner data, to be replaced with project data. Scope: 3 simply supported 35-ft bays, W33X387 girders, one 30-ton cab crane, on new freestanding W14X257 columns with welded twin-rib bracket seats, base plates, anchor rods and spread footings, and crane-level rod X-bracing; the existing building carries no crane load. Seismic: ordinary steel cantilever column system across the runway and rod bracing not specifically detailed for seismic resistance along it, Seismic Design Category B. A direct flange saddle does not suit this rolled girder (the sized saddle leaves flange-tie-saddle-weld 1.35, flange-tie-flange-fusion-weld 1.03 for the estimated tie demands): the paired flat bars bolt to the tie-side bearing stiffener, cut as one plate with its gusset extension past the flange tip (no weld at the gusset), the full-depth stiffener pair carrying the tie force into the girder. Bumper overhang assumed 20 in (end-wheel centerline to the extended bumper face, a typical supplier proportion): the stop contact positions use it; confirm with the crane supplier. The bracket stays: the W10X60 crane-level strut is moment-connected in plan at every column by 13 mm plates on its flanges (torsion brace, 5 rows of bolt pairs) and holds the new W14X257 columns against the twist: 0.0304 rad factored (limit 0.02) and 10 mm of bearing movement at every crane start and stop (limit 24 mm), still beyond a limit (column-twist or column-twist-rotation fails and stays in the calculation: a stiffer strut, a torsionally stiffer column or a column cap is needed). With the strut on the column centerline alone, the girder seated 945 mm off the column axis, the traction twists the column 0.3544 rad factored (limit 0.02) and 122 mm of bearing movement at every crane start and stop (limit 24 mm). The strut is sized so the girder's twist movement under the factored traction stays within 2 mm (a configurator target, tightened from 1/8 in where the tie could not take the movement, so the tie, slots and gaps are not sized by it).

Set by the tie sizing: the column face moves out from 20 in (to at most 30 in) until the tie passes its imposed-movement and strength checks.

fabrication.steel: Girder ASTM A992; plates, bars and stiffeners ASTM A572 Grade 50 unless noted.
fabrication.bolting: ASTM F3125 Grade A325, pretensioned, Class B faying surfaces, standard holes unless slots are detailed. Sliding-end bearing bolts and column-end tie bolts pretensioned against steel sleeves. Rail joints tight (gap 1/16 in max.), supplier's joint bars (deferred submittal) installed slip-critical: Class A surfaces, bolts pretensioned, re-tightened at 30 and 90 days.
fabrication.welding: E70XX low-hydrogen electrodes per AWS D1.1/D1.1M:2020, cyclically loaded provisions. Continuous fillets as dimensioned; no intermittent welds on cyclic load paths. Smooth starts and stops.
fabrication.inspection: Visual inspection of all welds; AWS D1.1/D1.1M:2020 cyclically loaded acceptance criteria; magnetic particle testing of fillets at fatigue-sensitive attachments; 100% ultrasonic testing of CJP welds; bolt pretension verification per RCSC.
fabrication.erection: Set and level the bearings, install the end bearings and flange ties, then set the rails. Provide temporary restraint until the permanent ties are complete.
fabrication.railAlignment: Set the rails to the specified gauge, alignment and level tolerances and survey them after erection, before the load test.
